results.summary: This design implements a washing machine controller using a finite state machine in Verilog. It simulates a simplified washing process with stages controlled by start, mode select, and door closed inputs. External hardware includes LEDs, a debounced button, and levers. The project is a straightforward educational example of an FSM for a household appliance.

This design implements a simple 8-bit SUBNEG CPU that interfaces with external parallel SRAM for program and data memory. It requires external components such as SRAM, address latches, and an output latch, and the program must be loaded into SRAM before enabling the CPU. The CPU provides internal state outputs for debugging. It is a minimal CPU architecture suitable for learning about processor internals.

This design implements a basic oscilloscope and signal generator on an ASIC using VHDL. It samples an external ADC, buffers data on FRAM, and displays the waveform via an HDMI Pmod, while also generating test signals (sine, square, triangle, sawtooth) through a DAC. The oscilloscope supports single-shot triggering with adjustable level and edge, and settings are output via UART. The project requires several external Pmods (ADC, DAC, FRAM, HDMI, buttons, switches) and is notable for its integration of multiple analog and digital peripherals.

This design implements a 'fastest finger' game that detects which of eight buttons is pressed first and lights the corresponding LED. It is built using Wokwi and is a simple combinational logic circuit. The project requires only buttons and LEDs for testing. It is a straightforward demonstration of priority encoding.

This design provides a set of analog multiplexers using passgates, configurable as 4:1 or 8:1 muxes, along with a ring oscillator and counter for testing. It includes manually laid out digital control logic and an OpenLane-generated counter to drive the mux at high frequencies. The project is intended for characterizing passgate performance and adding debug/inspection capability to analog designs. External analog test equipment is required for full characterization.

This design implements a Brokaw bandgap voltage reference that produces a stable ~1.2V output and includes a PTAT current generator for temperature readout. It uses SKY130 PNP BJTs and an OTA-based summing amplifier. The circuit requires only a 1.8V supply and no external components. It is suitable for characterizing temperature stability from -40°C to 125°C.

This design implements a simple I2C master controller that transmits one byte to a fixed slave address (0x50). It generates START and STOP conditions and provides BUSY, DONE, and ACK status outputs. The controller is tested by asserting START with an 8-bit data value on the inputs. External hardware such as an I2C slave device or logic analyzer is needed to observe the SDA and SCL signals.

This design wraps a high-speed crystal oscillator (HSXO) IP block from Chipalooza 2024 into the Tiny Tapeout analog template. It requires an external passive crystal, load capacitors, and a bias current generator to produce a clock output on the digital pin DOUT. The oscillator supports crystals between 4 and 16 MHz, with higher frequencies needing careful PCB layout. The project is a test chip for the HSXO IP.

This design reads up to six external photodiodes as digital inputs and displays the count of illuminated sensors on a 7-segment display. It can be tested with dip switches instead of photodiodes, and includes a mode switch for step or continuous sampling. The project is a simple sensor interface demonstration built with Wokwi. External hardware includes photodiodes, resistors, and a breadboard.

This design implements a 52-entry 6-bit FIFO using a chain of latches for the first 48 entries and a ring of flip-flops for the last 4, allowing random access to the oldest entries via a peek address. The FIFO provides ready, empty, and data outputs, and supports write, pop, and peek operations. Due to the latch chain, writes may be delayed after a pop when the FIFO is nearly full. The project is an educational example of FIFO implementation with mixed storage elements.
